descriptionChirho: A physical structure used as a residence, shelter, or meeting place — including singular and plural forms, all pronominal suffixes and prepositional combinations; Arabic بَيْت (bayt), Korean 집 (jip), and Swahili nyumba uniformly render this core architectural sense across all grammatical inflections.

The people belonging to or descended from a house, a family lineage or royal dynasty (e.g. 'house of David' = Davidic dynasty); Hindi distinctively renders this sense as घराना/घराने (gharana — clan, lineage) rather than घर/भवन (building), while Arabic بَيْت retains the same form but shifts to a collective-kinship reading.

Spatial or directional sense meaning 'inside, from within, inward' — a semantic extension from the enclosed space of a house to interiority itself; Arabic shifts to دَاخِل (dakhil — interior) rather than بَيْت, Korean uses 안 (an — inside) rather than 집, and Swahili uses ndani (inside) rather than nyumba, confirming this as a distinct lexical sense.

The Jerusalem Temple as the dwelling place of God, where target languages shift to temple-specific vocabulary: Hindi मंदिर (mandir), Spanish templo, distinguishing this referential sense from ordinary 'house'; Arabic الْبَيْت retains the same lexeme (cf. البيت الحرام for the Kaaba).
